data.Name: TP-03 | Trusted Relationship
data.Source: X3M.AI Threat Profile - System Integrator - TP-03 Customer Environment Pivot / Trusted Relationship
data.Description: Abuse an existing supplier, system-integrator, MSP, delegated administration or other trusted third-party relationship to gain access to a downstream customer environment. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: This is the defining technique for TP-03. A system integrator may legitimately hold customer accounts, GDAP relationships, VPN access, support identities, service accounts or other trusted administration paths. If the integrator or one of those identities is compromised, the attacker may inherit a route that receives less scrutiny than ordinary external access. Applicability: Core. Primary assets/relationships at risk: Customer tenant, Customer cloud subscriptions, Delegated administration relationships, Managed-service access paths, Customer privileged identities. Attack-path stage: Customer Entry. Detection opportunities: Correlate third-party/partner authentication with subsequent privileged activity; Monitor unusual customer access by partner identities, source IPs, devices and times; Review new or changed delegated relationships. Defensive considerations: Use least-privileged GDAP and customer roles; Time-bound access; Customer approval and periodic relationship review; Separate privileged identities; Revoke unused supplier access.

data.Name: TP-03 | External Remote Services

data.Description: Use legitimate external remote-access services such as VPN, Citrix, externally reachable WinRM/VNC or similar customer access mechanisms with compromised supplier or customer credentials. Why it matters for a system integrator/MSP: System integrators frequently receive customer-specific remote access. A compromised named or shared support account can therefore provide direct customer entry without exploitation of the public perimeter. Applicability: Remote Access / Conditional. Primary assets/relationships at risk: Customer VPN, Remote access gateways, Support infrastructure, Internal customer resources. Attack-path stage: Customer Entry. Detection opportunities: Successful remote access after unusual failures; New geolocation/device for supplier account; Access outside expected support windows; Remote access followed by internal discovery. Defensive considerations: MFA; Named accounts instead of shared accounts; Source restrictions; Session recording where appropriate; Time-bound enablement; Regular access review.

Detection opportunities: Privileged account disable/delete; Bulk role removal; Unexpected password reset or auth-method removal. Defensive considerations: Protected emergency access accounts; Out-of-band recovery; Alert on privileged-user removal; Separate recovery identities.
